title: Architecture review — multi-variant routing standup notes
content:
Meeting: Architecture review + weekly standup for multi-variant routing prototype
Date: 2026-03-09
Attendees: Ava Martinez (owner), Ravi Patel, Lena Cho, Miguel Rivera, Samir Gupta, Jules Park (notes), guest: Priya Nair (product)
Duration: 60min
Location: Zoom + #eng-serving-runtime

Agenda:
- Quick recap of RFC goals (5 min)
- Review prototype behavior: routing decisions, fallbacks, and admission control (20 min)
- KV cache/precision compatibility concerns (10 min)
- Telemetry and SLO impact modelling (10 min)
- Decide on integration approach and immediate next steps (15 min)

Recap of RFC goals (Ava):
- Implement a smart routing layer that can: route requests across model variants (full, quantized, distilled), route across heterogeneous GPU types (A100, H100, L40s), and enforce per-request budget and latency SLOs.
- Provide predictable degradation: if preferred variant not available, fall back to a compatible variant while preserving semantics when possible.
- Keep incremental rollout surface small (control-plane policy first, runtime shims second).

Prototype behavior summary (Ravi):
- Running a lightweight policy engine (k8s sidecar for now) that consults per-customer policy table.
- Policy inputs: requested model id, max_latency_ms, cost_budget_cents, region, customer_tier.
- Output: target variant id, preferred GPU class, fallback plan (ordered list).
- Runtime shim accepts assigned variant and either executes locally or proxies to other node pool.
- Admission control: simple token-bucket per node pool to avoid overload.

Discussion points and notes:
1) Policy placement tradeoffs:
   - Option A: Control-plane centralized policy service (single source of truth). Pros: easier rollout, simpler visibility. Cons: extra RTT, single point to scale.
   - Option B: Distributed policy caches colocated with routing proxies. Pros: lower latency; Cons: complexity in policy invalidation.
   - Decision: Move forward with centralized policy service for MVP but implement versioned policy blobs and an LRU cache in proxies so we can move to hybrid later.

2) Fallback compatibility and output quality:
   - Concern: Quantized vs full FP models can produce different outputs; some customers require exact-match behavior.
   - Proposal: Expose a policy flag `strict_semantics=true|false` per route. If true, only exact variant matches allowed (or manual approval for model substitution). If false, fallback to compatible quantized/distilled variants.
   - Action: Product to update route-level config to include `strict_semantics`. Owner: Priya. Due: 2026-03-18.

3) KV cache and context reuse across variants:
   - Problem: KV cache encodings differ for quantized kernels and some memory layouts differ by kernel. Reusing prefix cache across variant changes may corrupt decoding or give bad logits.
   - Short-term mitigation: Invalidate KV cache whenever the routing decision changes variant family (e.g., FP32 -> int8). This preserves correctness but has latency cost for new requests.
   - Long-term: Investigate normalized cache representation or on-the-fly conversion layers.
   - Action: Prototype a cache invalidation flag in runtime. Owner: Lena. Due: 2026-03-25.

4) Cost & SLO modelling (Miguel):
   - Ran simulation on last 7 days of traffic (sampled): allowing fallbacks to quantized variants reduced expected token cost by ~28% for 99th percentile latency unchanged in region-bound scenarios.
   - Risk: Burstload spikes can push fallback to lower-quality variants; need clear telemetry to detect regressions.
   - Decision: Add explicit tags in traces when fallback occurs so quality monitoring (Optimize) can correlate to evals.
   - Action: Instrument tracing to add `routing.variant.choice` and `routing.fallback_reason`. Owner: Miguel. Due: 2026-03-20.

5) Admission control and preemption policy (Samir):
   - Need to handle tenant isolation: reserved nodes for dedicated customers must not be preempted by hosted fallback routing.
   - Proposed rule: dedicated_capacity > hosted_fallback_priority. Also add a cost-based preemption for non-SLA traffic.
   - Action: Draft the preemption priority table and run tabletop scenarios. Owner: Samir. Due: 2026-03-22.

6) Canary/rollout strategy:
   - Canary approach: start with internal alpha customers -> opt-in external customers -> default off for public.
   - Canary tests: unit tests, integration with cache invalidation, and an e2e latency/cost bench with synthetic workload.
   - Action: Create canary test plan doc and list customers. Owner: Jules. Due: 2026-03-17.

Decisions made (summary):
- Centralized policy service for MVP with a versioned policy blob and small local cache in routing proxies. (Owner: Ava)
- Expose `strict_semantics` at route-level; default = false. Product will add to route config. (Owner: Priya)
- Invalidate KV cache across variant-family changes for correctness in MVP; pursue normalized cache research separately. (Owner: Lena)
- Instrument traces and metrics for fallback detection. (Owner: Miguel)
- Define preemption priority rules to protect dedicated capacity. (Owner: Samir)

Unresolved/open questions:
- How expensive will normalized cache conversion be in practice? Do we need hardware support? (research)
- Should per-request cost budgets be enforced by rejecting requests or by dynamically selecting variants? (policy semantics)
- Are there edge cases where semantic guarantees require partial re-computation rather than full cache invalidation?

Action items (concrete list):
- Priya: Update route config schema to include `strict_semantics` and publish product note. Due 2026-03-18.
- Lena: Implement runtime flag to invalidate KV cache on variant-family change; add test cases. Due 2026-03-25.
- Miguel: Add routing fields to traces and link to Optimize dashboards. Due 2026-03-20.
- Samir: Draft preemption priority table and run 3 tabletop scenarios. Due 2026-03-22.
- Jules: Draft canary test plan and coordinate alpha customers. Due 2026-03-17.
- Ava/Ravi: Build small throughput benchmark for mixed-variant routing and run on H100 and A100 pools. Due 2026-03-24.
- Engineering: Create JIRA epic JIRA-INF-2741 to track work and split into stories (owners assign).

Follow-ups and next meeting:
- Weekly sync on this RFC in the normal eng-weekly slot; short async updates on PR progress.
- Next focused deep-dive on cache normalization strategy scheduled for 2026-03-23 (30 min). Owner: Lena.

Notes to self / rough ideas captured during meeting (informal):
- Could we add a fast-path for short prompt prefix hits where we always pick the cheapest variant if prefix matched last 5 requests? Risky but could be big cost win.
- Consider adding a per-tenant override UI in Console so SRE/SEs can opt a customer into strict semantics temporarily.
- Need to coordinate with security for any proxying across regions (data residency).

References mentioned:
- adaptive-routing RFC draft: https://confluence.redwood/INF/rfc/adaptive-routing-2026
- JIRA-INF-2741 (epic)
- PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/serving-runtime/pull/812

End of notes.
